facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of pain and swelling around his right ankle
bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
the ankle and subtalar joints had a full range of motion
Complete blood count was within normal limits
erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
a diagnosis of Brodie’s abscess was made
curettage was performed under spinal anesthesia via an anterior approach
curetted material was sent for histopathological and microbiological assessment

concepts.why: The patient's 1-year history of pain and swelling around the ankle, bony thickening, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and radiographic findings of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin are consistent with Brodie's abscess.
The patient's symptoms and radiographic findings are consistent with osteomyelitis, although the specific diagnosis of Brodie's abscess is more precise.

The patient's symptoms and radiographic findings could be consistent with Ewing's sarcoma, although the absence of other characteristic features and the presence of a well-defined sclerotic margin make this diagnosis less likely.
The patient's symptoms and radiographic findings could be consistent with osteoid osteoma, although the size and location of the lesion are not typical for this diagnosis.

The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are consistent with chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis, although the radiographic findings and lack of other characteristic features make this diagnosis less likely.
